# World assets are generated by Blender at build time, and only the scripts are committed

The world's models and textures (room and corridor kits, desk sets, robots, clutter, and their baked tileable textures) are produced by Python scripts run in headless Blender, kept in `desktop/world-assets/`. Only those scripts are committed; the `.glb` files and PNG textures are regenerated by the build before `tauri dev` and `tauri build`, skipped when a fingerprint of the scripts is unchanged, and shipped as files beside the app. The only committed files the scripts don't produce are third-party ones that cannot be generated (the sign font), each with a note of its source and licence. Decided with the effort owner on 2026-10-17 ([How assets are made, kept and shipped](../../.scratch/sweatshop-rooms/issues/06-grilling-how-assets-are-made-and-shipped.md)), so that the repo holds the source of every asset rather than its binary output.

## Considered Options

- **Committing the generated `.glb` files and textures:** builders would not need Blender, but the repo would carry tens of megabytes of binary output that drifts from its scripts. Rejected by the owner.
- **Hand-made assets in the Blender editor:** not reproducible from text and not reviewable in a diff.

## Consequences

- Every machine that builds the desktop app needs Blender 4.3.x and numpy (Debian's package also needs `python3-numpy`). The build checks both and stops with a clear message if either is missing; the minor is pinned so bakes match across machines.
- A first build, or any change to a script, bakes about 30 textures and takes minutes.
- The scripts must be deterministic: the same scripts on the same Blender minor must produce the same output.
